public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says LLMs were still hallucinating as of late 2025. Vectara's leaderboard, published on 19 November 2025, tested models on how faithfully they summarize. It reported that Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5, GPT-OSS-120B, Grok-4 and DeepSeek-R1 each had a hallucination rate above 10%. The lowest rate on that benchmark was 3.3%, for Gemini-2.5-flash-lite, so no model it tested reached zero. In a paper posted on 4 September 2025, OpenAI researchers wrote that hallucinations persist even in state-of-the-art systems. Together these support the observable part of the claim for the September to December 2025 period. The stronger reading, that LLMs can never stop hallucinating, is not tested here. The same OpenAI paper argues that hallucinations could be reduced by changing how benchmarks are scored.
limitations: The Vectara figures come from one benchmark of summarization faithfulness. They may not reflect other tasks or other ways of measuring factual accuracy.
The evidence covers only the models these two sources name or describe. It does not show results for every frontier model released in late 2025.
The GPT-5.2 system card (December 2025) could not be read, so its hallucination figures are not included.
This grade covers whether hallucination persisted in late 2025. It does not cover the claim that hallucination can never be eliminated.

from_speaker: listed as an essay title from 2025 recommended for rereading
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post date, current LLMs, including frontier models, still produce hallucinations (plausible but false content) at measurable, non-trivial rates, and no model has eliminated them.

The phrase 'can't stop' also hints at an inherent, permanent limit. That stronger theoretical point cannot be settled by observation. This assessment checks only the observable part: whether hallucination persisted in state-of-the-art models in late 2025.
criteria.support_condition: Independent benchmarks or developer research from late 2025 show that leading LLMs still hallucinate at non-trivial rates.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence from late 2025 shows that frontier LLMs had reliably eliminated hallucinations, with near-zero rates across standard factuality and faithfulness tests.
